title: A Quiet Week With a Hole in the New Index
titleEmphasis: A hole in the new index.
deck: IHSG slipped 0.13% to 5,050.429 while Taiwan, Korea and Japan fell 9% to 12% in an AI sell-off. Foreign selling nearly stopped. In the first week of the cleaned index, a stock 99.64% held by a few accounts added 12.40 points. October was the worst month of 33 markets. We stay defensive.
description: Indonesia weekly research for 2 to 6 November 2026 with an October review. Audited IDX data, the MKNT case in the cleaned index, the global AI sell-off, October's 16.70% fall against 33 markets, sukuk demand and a check of last week's call.

sections.title: Asia fell hard. Jakarta barely moved. We still would not buy it.

blocks.text: IHSG slipped 0.13% to 5,050.429, a loss of 6.621 points. In the same week Taiwan's index fell 12.19%, Korea's KOSPI 11.71% and Japan's Nikkei 9.25%. A flat week next to a crash looks like strength. We read it differently. Indonesia has almost none of the AI hardware makers that were sold, so the storm went round it, and the flat number hides a split inside the market.

Large banks rose and small stocks fell. LQ45 gained 0.60% and financials 1.33%, while the IDX SMC Composite lost 3.08% and the Acceleration Board 7.00%. By count, 579 stocks fell and 215 rose. BBCA alone added 20.48 points, and it was the stock foreign investors bought most, by an estimated Rp520bn. Foreign selling across all stocks nearly stopped, at Rp167bn against Rp3.06tn the week before.

The second name on IDX's list of leaders is the one that bothers us. MKNT, a stock at Rp32, added 12.40 points. That is more than the whole index lost. A week earlier it traded at Rp11, and on 16 October at Rp1. On Friday evening IDX and KSEI published a notice saying a limited number of holders control 99.64% of its shares. This was the first week of the index without the 81 concentrated stocks that left on 2 November, and a stock with the same problem did the heavy lifting. Without MKNT the index would have fallen about 19 points, or 0.38%.

Our view stays defensive. Foreign selling has paused and sukuk demand improved, and those are real changes. But foreigners still sold BBRI and BMRI, the index rose on a stock with almost no free float in practice, and October left the market 16.70% lower in a month in which most of the world was steady. We would turn neutral if foreign investors buy the large banks for two weeks in a row, if a conventional bond auction draws strong bids for long tenors, and if IHSG closes above 5,488.

blocks.label: Checking last week's call
blocks.text: Last week we set three tests. The first was a bond auction with strong bids. The sukuk auction on Tuesday drew Rp28.56tn of bids, 25.5% more than the one before, but 73.67% of them were for short-term bills. That is half a pass. The second was an end to foreign selling of TLKM, BMRI and BBRI. TLKM passed, with estimated net selling of Rp12bn against Rp1.19tn. BMRI and BBRI did not, at Rp219bn and Rp399bn. The third was a close above 5,488 with foreign buying. The best close was 5,096.830 on Monday. The week stayed inside our planning range of 4,437 to 5,185, between a low of 4,824.364 and a high of 5,143.582.

sections.title: One bad Tuesday and a recovery

blocks.label: Exhibit 01
blocks.title: A 3.78% fall on Tuesday, then three higher closes
blocks.note: Select a date to inspect the closing observation. Lines join daily closes and show no intraday highs or lows.

event.label: Wall Street's AI sell-off
event.note: Thursday 5 November in New York, after the Jakarta close. Asia fell on Friday

blocks.text: Monday opened the cleaned index with a rise of 0.79% to 5,096.830. On Tuesday IHSG reached 5,143.582, the high of the week, then fell 4.65% from that point to close at 4,904.287, down 3.78% on the day. BBRI fell 5.67% and foreign investors sold a net Rp575bn, the most of any day this week. We found no filing or data release that explains Tuesday. Wednesday touched the week's low of 4,824.364 before closing up 0.32%.

Thursday brought the biggest rise, 2.25% to 5,030.261. BPS published third-quarter growth of 5.47% that day. We cannot show the release moved the market, only that they share a date. On Friday, while Tokyo, Seoul and Taipei fell, IHSG rose 0.40% to 5,050.429, its high of the day, and foreign investors bought a net Rp328bn.

Trading thinned again. Total value averaged Rp11.04tn a day, 23.00% less than the week before, and regular-market value averaged Rp9.43tn, down 26.79%. Negotiated trades were 14.60% of the week's value. Foreign investors were 37% of trading, down from 41%.

Measured by value, the picture is less one-sided. Stocks worth Rp4,624tn fell and stocks worth Rp3,469tn rose, 53.24% and 39.94% of the value in IDX's chart. Many small stocks fell and a few large ones rose. IDX again printed the percentages of the two falling groups in each other's place, in both bars, so we recompute every share from the counts.

sections.title: A stock at Rp32 did more for the index than the market did

rows: Shares held by a few holders, KSEI
blocks.caption: From IDX weekly pages 4 and 5, the IDX company profile, the 6 November HSC notice and the frozen daily rows

blocks.text: MKNT came back from a trading halt on 19 October at Rp2. It then rose by one rupiah a day for nine sessions, to Rp11 on 30 October. At such prices each rupiah is a large step in percentage terms. This week the steps grew: Rp14, Rp18, Rp24 and Rp32. On Friday no share traded at all. IDX's own October report lists MKNT as the month's top gainer, up 1,000%.

The index counts MKNT at its registered free float. The register shows 19.955% of shares held by the public, 205.5bn shares, worth Rp6.58tn at Rp32. That matches IDX's free-float value on page 5, and it is why a stock with Rp28.3bn of trading in the week could add 12.40 points. KSEI's count tells a different story. As of 5 November, a limited number of holders controlled 99.64% of all MKNT shares, which means most of the shares the register calls public sit with a few accounts too.

IDX asked the company to explain the trading on 4 November. Its answer on 6 November said it knew of no undisclosed material facts, had received no reports of shareholder activity and was not buying its own shares. The rise has no stated cause. Foreign investors were almost absent, with estimated net buying of Rp0.22bn.

blocks.label: Our assessment
blocks.text: The cleaned index was meant to stop thin, concentrated stocks from moving IHSG. In its first week a thin, concentrated stock was its second largest support. IDX has not said whether MKNT will leave the index before the current evaluation period ends on 29 January 2027. The new rule of 2 November, which adds controller status to holdings above 1% in monthly reports, will help investors see such cases. It does not change the index on its own. Until the index rules catch up with the HSC notices, we will report IHSG's move with and without stocks like this.

blocks.label: Exhibit 02
blocks.title: Net selling of Rp167bn, with buying on two days
blocks.note: Official all-market stock trading, foreign purchases less sales. This measures trading, not money leaving the country.

blocks.text: The week's net selling of Rp167bn was 94.53% smaller than the Rp3.06tn of the week before. Wednesday and Friday were days of net buying. The total for 2026 is Rp98.09tn. Domestic investors bought Rp35.04tn and sold Rp34.87tn, close to balance.

Our stock-level estimate covers 79 liquid large caps with at least Rp10tn of market value and Rp10bn of average daily trading. It shows foreign investors buying BBCA, by Rp520bn, and ASII, by Rp269bn. For ASII that buying was unusually large against its own last 120 sessions. They sold BBRI, by Rp399bn, BMRI, by Rp219bn, and GOTO, ANTM and ADRO by Rp116bn to Rp125bn each. The estimate values foreign share volume at each day's close and leaves out negotiated trades. For all stocks it comes to Rp688bn of net selling, Rp521bn more than the official figure, so we use it only to see which stocks foreigners traded.

sections.title: Banks rose and small stocks fell

blocks.label: Exhibit 03
blocks.title: Five laggards and five leaders
blocks.note: Official weekly IHSG contributions from IDX. The full ten leaders added 80.78 points and the ten laggards took away 46.51.

blocks.text: BBCA rose 4.42% and added 20.48 points. ASII, SMMA, CASA and INDF followed. BRPT was the largest drag. It fell about 6.7% on each of the last four days and lost 20.56% in the week, costing 15.98 points. Its last filings were nine-month results on 30 October and a notice of a public expose on 5 November. We found nothing that explains the fall. AADI, UNTR, PTBA, MEDC and ENRG put coal and energy among the laggards.

blocks.label: Exhibit 04
blocks.title: Two sectors rose and nine fell
blocks.note: Weekly price changes of the IDX sector indices.

blocks.text: Financials rose 1.33% and consumer non-cyclicals 0.85%. Technology lost 6.46%, transport 5.35% and energy 5.01%. The Main Board fell 0.76%, the Development Board 2.79% and the Acceleration Board 7.00%. IDX High Dividend 20 gained 0.66% and IDX BUMN20 0.68%. The more liquid and the larger the stock, the better it did.

sections.title: The AI sell-off went round Indonesia

blocks.label: Exhibit 05
blocks.title: North Asia fell hardest, India rose most
blocks.note: Asian changes from IDX's global table, Friday to Friday. US changes from FRED and CNBC closes, also Friday to Friday, because IDX's table stops at the Thursday close in New York.

blocks.text: The trigger came from the United States. Democrats won the midterm elections on 3 November, and some of the winners had promised to slow new data centres, among them the governor-elect of Texas. On Thursday the S&P 500 fell 4.36%, the Nasdaq Composite 5.52% and the Nasdaq 100, which holds the largest technology companies, 6.36%. Reuters and NBC both trace the fall to fears of tighter rules for AI on top of doubts about the returns on data-centre spending. Friday brought a small recovery in New York, with the S&P 500 up 0.31%. Over the full week the S&P 500 lost 2.68%, the Nasdaq Composite 3.37% and the Dow 0.94%.

Asia took the hit on Friday. The Nikkei fell 5.96% that day, Reuters and NBC both report heavy losses in Seoul, and Taiwan's index ended the week 12.19% lower. These are the markets that make the chips and memory for American data centres, which NBC's sources stress and Reuters echoes when it explains why India escaped. India went the other way, with its best week in six years according to Reuters, and the SENSEX rose 8.82%. In Southeast Asia, Singapore fell 3.67% and Thailand 3.48%. Indonesia lost 0.13%, and Malaysia and the Philippines rose.

blocks.caption: US figures from FRED and CNBC. Others from IDX's weekly and October tables. European weeks end on Thursday
Yields from the US Treasury, Brent settlements from Reuters, JISDOR from Bank Indonesia

blocks.text: Oil fell for a different reason. On Monday Brent dropped 7.63% after Iran said talks to end the war with the United States and Israel were continuing, as both Reuters and the Guardian reported. It ended the week at 98.32 dollars, 13.32% below its 113.43 close of 30 October. Cheaper oil eases the fuel subsidy bill the KSSK statement mentions, but it also takes away support from the coal and energy stocks that led IDX's laggards. American payrolls rose 165,000 in October, and US yields ended the week lower.

sections.title: October was the worst month of 33 markets

blocks.label: Exhibit 06
blocks.title: Indonesia fell 16.70% in October, the most in IDX's table
blocks.note: Monthly changes from page 20 of IDX's October statistics. IDX names countries, not indices. Its US figure matches the Dow from 30 September to 29 October.

blocks.text: IHSG fell from 6,071.138 to 5,057.050 in October, a loss of 16.70% and 1,014.088 points. Among the 33 markets in IDX's monthly table it came last, just behind Korea at -16.19%. Most of the world was calm. The Dow rose 1.70% over the full month, the S&P 500 slipped 0.93% and Japan lost 5.19%. Since January IHSG is down 41.52%, again the worst in the table, while Taiwan is up 56.10%. In dollars, with JISDOR moving from 17,877 to 18,138, IHSG lost about 17.90% in the month.

blocks.caption: From pages 1, 14 and 15 of IDX's October statistics

blocks.text: The month broke on one day. MSCI announced at 03:40 Jakarta time on 16 October that it would consult on moving Indonesia out of its emerging markets index into standalone status. IHSG fell 11.57% that day, from 5,863.780 to 5,185.105. Foreign investors sold a net Rp16.88tn in the month, 17.24% of the year's total, and IDX's market value shrank by Rp1,833tn. The Financial System Stability Committee's statement of 3 November names the same causes we saw: energy prices driven by the war in the Middle East, tight policy abroad, tighter liquidity at home, the MSCI announcement and outflows from shares.

blocks.label: Exhibit 07
blocks.title: Every sector fell in October
blocks.note: One-month changes of the IDX sector indices from page 18 of the October statistics.

blocks.text: Infrastructure lost 26.02%, basic materials 23.90% and industrials 22.91%. Financials held up best at -8.41%. BBCA fell 18.02% and cost the index 99.71 points, the largest single drag. The ten largest laggards together took 446.95 points, 44.07% of the month's fall, and six of them were BYAN, BRMS, BREN, MORA, DSSA and MDKA, stocks that fell 22% to 51%. The Acceleration Board lost 33.04%. IDX Value30 lost only 4.87%, the best of IDX's indices. Value stocks held up far better than the rest of the market.

Sukuk demand improved. At Tuesday's auction investors bid Rp28.56tn, up 25.5% from Rp22.76tn, and the government took Rp16.65tn, above its Rp10tn target. Bloomberg Technoz and Kontan report the same figures. The detail matters. Rp21.04tn of the bids, 73.67%, were for short-term SPNS bills, and Kontan's source says long tenors still drew little interest. Investors will lend to the government for months, not yet for years. Last week's conventional auction drew only Rp31.09tn of bids, so one sukuk auction does not change the picture.

The rupiah hardly moved. JISDOR ended the week at 18,130, 0.04% stronger than on 30 October. In dollars IHSG lost about 0.09%. At home, BPS reported growth of 5.47% from a year earlier in the third quarter and October inflation of 3.23%. The economy is not where the trouble lies. The trouble is in the trust investors place in how the market is run, which is what MSCI questioned.

blocks.caption: Our tests for the coming weeks

blocks.text: The downside test is simple. A close below 4,824.364, this week's low, would most likely come through the large banks, because they now carry more of the index. Their foreign selling is the thing to watch, more than the headline level.
